hook.line: Tomás has to tell a lawyer what Yesid said. In news and statements, people write *dijo ser inocente* instead of *dijo que era inocente*. You will read it far more than you say it.

examples.en: He claims to be a doctor.
The detainee said he was innocent.

examples.es: Yesid asegura no conocer a ese hombre.
examples.en: Yesid insists he does not know that man.

examples.es: Ella afirma ser la dueña del local.
examples.en: She claims to be the owner of the premises.

examples.es: Los vecinos aseguraron no saber nada.
examples.en: The neighbours insisted they knew nothing.

rule:
When the person who speaks is also the person described, you can skip *que* and the second verb's ending. *Dijo que era inocente* becomes *dijo ser inocente*.

Use it after *decir, afirmar, asegurar, reconocer, negar*. *No* goes before the infinitive: *afirmó no saber*.

Different people? Keep *que*: *dijo que Rosa era la dueña*.

In everyday talk, *dijo que era* is more natural. *Dice ser* sounds like a report.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an infinitive clause with the same subject. The infinitive replaces *que* plus a conjugated verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *ser* or *es*: Dice ___ abogado. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.why: With the same person speaking and described, the infinitive *ser* replaces *que es*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *no saber* or *saber no*: Afirmó ___ nada. Type the whole sentence.
Type in Spanish: He claims to be a doctor.
yourTurn.why: *Decir, afirmar* and *asegurar* all take the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Yesid insists he does not know that man.
yourTurn.answer: Yesid asegura no conocer a ese hombre.
accept: Yesid afirma no conocer a ese hombre.
yourTurn.why: Same person, so *no conocer* instead of *que no conoce*.

yourTurn.prompt: Rewrite with an infinitive: *Dijo que era inocente.*
yourTurn.why: The same person speaks and is described, so *que era* shrinks to *ser*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Afirmó saber la verdad.*
Type in Spanish: Marta said that Rosa was the owner.
yourTurn.answer: Marta dijo que Rosa era la dueña.
yourTurn.why: A different person is described, so you need *que* and a full verb.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Use either *que* plus a full verb, or the infinitive alone, not both.
Almost. *No* goes before the infinitive, as before any verb.
Almost. A job after *ser* drops the English "a".

personal: Think of someone who claims something about themselves, and say it with *dice ser…* or *asegura no…*.
